messages.content:
You are an expert synthetic chemist planning experiments to maximise reaction yield.
Each experiment chooses one option for every variable listed. You will see the results
of experiments already run. Choose the next batch to find the highest-yield conditions
in as few experiments as possible. Use chemical knowledge (ligand and base effects,
substrate reactivity, solvent effects) and the observed results. Balance exploiting
good regions with testing informative new combinations. Never repeat an experiment.
Return JSON only.

Pd-catalysed Buchwald-Hartwig amination of 3-chloropyridine with 4-methylaniline; choose the ligand, base and isoxazole additive.

Variables and options:

picks.reason: The lead ligand and base provide the strongest established platform, and this tests whether the dibenzylamino substituent is beneficial in the alternative isoxazole position.
This tests a fused benzisoxazole additive under the best-performing catalyst and base conditions.
This tests the regioisomeric fused benzisoxazole and can reveal whether its ring connectivity affects the additive effect.
This evaluates a methyl-substituted, ester-bearing isoxazole while retaining the best-performing catalyst and base.
This probes the regioisomer of the ester-bearing isoxazole to assess positional effects on the strong L2/B2 platform.
This tests a compact dimethylisoxazole additive and checks whether phenyl substitution is necessary for high yield.
This tests a heteroaryl-substituted isoxazole as a distinct additive class under the leading conditions.
This evaluates an ester-bearing isoxazole with a different substitution pattern from the previously tested additive.
This tests the unsubstituted 3-methylisoxazole analogue to assess the contribution of the substituents in the better-performing additives.
This tests an isoxazole-4-carboxylate additive to explore whether an electron-withdrawing ester supports the observed additive effect.
This tests the regioisomeric isoxazole-3-carboxylate under the best established conditions.
This probes a methoxy- and ester-substituted isoxazole while holding the catalyst and base at their current optima.
This tests a compact ester-substituted isoxazole to compare with the phenyl-containing additive that gave the highest yield.
This explores a furyl-substituted isoxazole ester as a heteroaryl analogue under the leading conditions.
This tests the thienyl analogue of A21 to assess whether heteroaryl identity changes the additive effect.
A5 performed well with L2/B2, so this tests whether the nearly comparable L1 ligand can improve that additive combination.
This checks whether the XPhos ligand can match the strong L2/B2/A5 result with a different ligand environment.
This isolates the AdBrettPhos ligand under the best-known base and additive conditions, unlike its prior low-yield result with different conditions.
This tests whether the strong B2 and competent L1 combination can improve on the moderate L2/B2/A14 result.
This compares XPhos with the other ligands using the same base and phenyl-substituted additive.
